summary.headline: BLOCK on 3 high findings: unbounded metric cardinality (unauthenticated memory exhaustion) and Prometheus exposition injection, both HTTP-reachable and proven live in the newly shipped GET /metrics; plus a sanitise_context bypass that passes registered PII through unfiltered on the int and mapping-key paths.

prior_block_disposition.SEC-001: closed - confirmed fixed; five different adversarial backtracking shapes all linear and sub-millisecond; the axis is clean, no ReDoS shape exists on this design
prior_block_disposition.SEC-002: closed - request-scoped design proven correct on both the async and the threadpool/context-copy handler paths; traceback logged, scrubbed and correlated; residual is the still-exported redact_values API (SEC-109)
prior_block_disposition.SEC-003: partially closed - string path is protected; int/bool values and mapping keys bypass scrubbing entirely (SEC-103, new BLOCK); credential-URI heuristic bypassable (SEC-108)
prior_block_disposition.SEC-004_005: unchanged at HEAD - re-rated medium; CRLF log injection and HTTP response splitting sub-claims explicitly refuted with evidence
prior_block_disposition.SEC-010_011: unchanged - advisories re-measured (SEC-111); lockfile is not merely uncommitted, it is gitignored at .gitignore:49 (SEC-112)

block_framing.note: Reachability was disputed in the prior round, so each BLOCK states whether an attacker can reach it at HEAD or whether it needs a later story to wire it up.
block_framing.latent_rationale: No file under backend/src/** calls register_sensitive or redact_values, or raises AppError; both are exercised only by tests. SEC-103 is filed at BLOCK anyway because the defective artefact is group A's own deliverable - the designated outbound PII control - and it was demonstrated passing registered PII through unmodified. The exploit is one downstream story away, not one attacker step away.

dependency_audit.downgrade_rationale: All 5 advisories are devDependency-only and absent from the built artefact. The npm-critical vitest GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp requires the Vitest UI server to be listening; the only script is 'vitest run' (no --ui, no watch), so the precondition is unmet. The npm-high vite GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff is a dev-server fs.deny bypass whose Windows precondition IS met, so the residual risk is real but limited to a developer workstation running npm run dev. npm's raw labels are preserved here so the downgrade is auditable.

advisories.precondition: vitest --ui server listening (not used by any script)

dependency_audit.backend_manifest_note: backend/pyproject.toml is not in the change set, so no Python dependency audit was run (scan step 5 skipped per scope rules).

findings.title: Unbounded metric cardinality gives an anonymous client unbounded process memory growth
findings.description: The RED counter is keyed on the raw request path rather than the matched route template, and _request_counts is a process-global collections.Counter with no bound, no TTL and no eviction (only a test-only reset helper). The increment happens in the http.response.start wrapper, so it fires for every response including 404s on paths that route nowhere. Every invented URL becomes a permanent key.
findings.evidence: Live uvicorn on port 8009: 100,000 unique 404 paths over one keep-alive connection in 18.6 s (~4,900 req/s) grew the GET /metrics body from 0 to 9.08 MB, strictly linear, zero eviction. tracemalloc over 200k keys measured 191 bytes retained per key (1M keys ~191 MB, 10M ~1.9 GB). Paths of 8,000 characters are accepted and still counted, so one key can retain ~8.2 KB; at the measured rate that is ~40 MB/s of unreclaimable heap from a single connection. GET /metrics also renders the whole snapshot into a list and joins it, so a 40-byte unauthenticated request already returns 9 MB (~47,000x amplification) and grows without bound. No rate limiting exists anywhere (SEC-122).
findings.fix: Key the counter on the matched route template (scope['route'].path after routing) and bucket anything unrouted under a single fixed '<unmatched>' label, so cardinality is a function of the route table. Add a hard ceiling on distinct keys as defence in depth, and prefer a real prometheus_client registry over a hand-rolled Counter.

findings.title: Prometheus exposition injection via an unescaped attacker-controlled path label
findings.description: The exposition line is built by f-string interpolation of the raw path into a quoted label value with no escaping of double quote, backslash or newline. ASGI scope['path'] is percent-decoded, so %22 and %0A in the request target arrive as a literal quote and a literal newline, giving an anonymous client control over line structure in the /metrics output.
findings.evidence: Proven against a real uvicorn server over raw HTTP (not only TestClient): one GET with a percent-encoded path payload caused GET /metrics to return a fully forged sample line with route="/forged", status="200" and a value of 424242. A plain %22 also breaks label quoting, which alone is enough to make a scraper reject the whole payload. Impact: forged counter names and values injected into the operator's time-series database, or corruption of the exposition so nothing ingests. This project's runtime-SLO sensor reads /metrics for the {error_rate_pct:1, p95_ms:500} SLO, so forged samples can mask a real breach.
findings.fix: Escape label values per the Prometheus exposition spec (backslash, double quote, newline) at render time, and - jointly with SEC-101 - stop using the raw path as a label so the value comes from a fixed route-table allow-list rather than from the request.

findings.title: sanitise_context bypass: int/bool values and mapping keys skip scrub_text entirely
findings.description: sanitise_context applies all three of its protections (credential-URI drop, 200-char cap, scrub_text) only on the str branch. _scalar returns int and bool values verbatim and they never see scrub_text - and Aadhaar, account and phone numbers are naturally ints. Separately, mapping keys are only str()-coerced at line 182: no scrub, no length cap, no credential-URI check, even though a PII value as a per-field error key is an ordinary shape.
findings.evidence: Demonstrated at HEAD. With register_sensitive('ABCDE1234F','234512345678') active and a 409 AppError, the response body shows the control firing and not firing in the same envelope: detail 'rejected for PAN [REDACTED]', context {'pan': '[REDACTED]', 'aadhaar_int': 234512345678, 'ABCDE1234F': 'pan-as-key'}. The registered Aadhaar egressed as an integer and the registered PAN egressed as a key, to an unauthenticated client, while the identical values were redacted one field away. Logs for the same request were clean, so this is purely the outbound-wire control - the exact channel SEC-003 was about.
findings.reachability_note: Not HTTP-reachable at HEAD: a change-set-scoped grep found no file under backend/src/** that raises AppError or calls register_sensitive. Reachable as soon as any group B/E story populates context, which is the field's documented purpose (src/types/errors.py cites E4-S4-AC2).
findings.fix: In _scalar, coerce non-string scalars through scrub_text(str(value)) and re-type only after scrubbing (keep Decimal -> str). In sanitise_context, run keys through the same pipeline as values, dropping a key that changes under scrubbing rather than emitting [REDACTED] as a key. Add a regression test registering a numeric Aadhaar and a PAN-as-key.

findings.title: lru_cache(maxsize=256) thrashes into a per-log-line regex recompilation DoS
findings.description: _scrub compiles a pattern per registered value through a 256-entry LRU. A sequential scan over more than 256 keys is the classic LRU worst case: the entry needed next is always the one just evicted, so the hit rate collapses to zero and every log line recompiles every pattern. Compilation cost is also linear in value length and unbounded.
findings.evidence: Measured per log line: 10 values 0.00 ms; 256 values 0.10 ms (cache full, 256 hits); 257 values 0.77 ms with 0 hits; 1000 values 95.18 ms with 0 hits and 2000 misses - a ~1000x regression at a threshold nothing enforces or warns about. Separately a 50,000-char registered value compiles a 650 KB pattern in 424 ms, and can never stay cached alongside others. A story registering per-token content from a parsed salary document, or a bulk endpoint registering values for many applicants in one request, reaches both conditions naturally. This is the alternative axis requested for SEC-001; it is a cache/compilation DoS, not a backtracking one.
findings.fix: Replace the global lru_cache with a per-request pattern cache held in the redaction scope (a dict beside the sensitive set in the contextvar), sized by that request's own registrations. Reject or truncate registrations above a sane length ceiling (PAN 10 chars, Aadhaar 12). The same change fixes SEC-105.

findings.title: Registered PII outlives the request scope inside the pattern cache
findings.description: The module contract is that registration is request-scoped and the correlation middleware owns the lifetime. The lru_cache silently breaks it: the cache key is the raw sensitive value and the cached re.Pattern embeds the escaped literal, so both survive end_redaction_scope. Up to 256 PANs, Aadhaars and document ids therefore sit in resident memory indefinitely, across requests and across users, reachable from a core dump, heap dump, crash reporter or any future introspection endpoint.
findings.evidence: After begin_redaction_scope / register_sensitive('ABCDE1234F') / scrub_text / end_redaction_scope, _sensitive_values.get() is None but _redaction_pattern('ABCDE1234F') is a cache HIT (hits incremented, cache_info currsize 256) - the PAN string is still live in the process. No cache keyed on the plaintext can avoid this, because the compiled pattern contains the value either way.
findings.fix: Use the per-request cache from SEC-104, which dies with the request context. If the global cache is kept for performance, call _redaction_pattern.cache_clear() from end_redaction_scope and accept recompilation.

findings.title: X-Request-ID accepted unbounded and unvalidated, reflected into every log line and the response
findings.description: The inbound header is taken verbatim with no length limit, no character allow-list and no shape check, then bound to the request-id contextvar, stamped on the response and written into every structured log line for the request.
findings.evidence: Live uvicorn: a 60,000-character X-Request-ID returns 200 and is echoed in full in the response header; uvicorn imposes no practical ceiling. An 8 KB id turned one trivial GET /health into 8,744 bytes of log output versus ~330 normally (~26x; ~190x at 60 KB) - cheap unauthenticated log-volume amplification against disk and any per-GB log pipeline, and the same knob that makes request tracing unusable. Prior SEC-004/005 sub-claims of CRLF log injection and response splitting are separately REFUTED (see refuted_candidates).
findings.fix: Validate on ingress: accept the inbound id only if it matches a strict allow-list such as ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$, otherwise generate a fresh uuid4().hex and ignore the caller's value. Never echo an unvalidated caller string in a response header.

findings.owasp: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
findings.title: Correlation id is caller-controlled, enabling audit-trail forgery and collision
findings.description: Because any client can set the id, any client can choose it: replay another request's id to interleave their own actions into that trace, collide every request onto one id to destroy correlation, or pick an id that impersonates an internal caller's format. For a loan-origination platform whose Correlation Id is the audit-trail spine (specs/design/CONTEXT.md), that is an integrity defect, not merely an observability one - a log record can no longer be trusted to attribute an action to a requester.
findings.evidence: middleware.py:86-87 reads the inbound header and falls back to uuid4().hex only when it is absent. Verified live: X-Request-ID: req-abc is adopted verbatim and appears as request_id on the access log line and in the response header. Note QA-VM-003 in the frozen contract requires this echo behaviour, so the fix must preserve the echo while removing the trust.
findings.fix: Either generate the id server-side unconditionally, or trust an inbound id only from an authenticated internal peer and record it in a separate field (upstream_request_id) while keeping the server-generated request_id authoritative.

findings.title: _CREDENTIAL_URI allow-list is bypassable; credentials still egress in context
findings.description: The regex models exactly one credential shape (scheme, then user, colon, password, at-sign, host) and its password character class forbids a slash, so a password containing '/' defeats detection. Non-URI credential formats are not modelled at all.
findings.evidence: Both confirmed egressing from a live 409 envelope at HEAD: a postgresql-scheme DSN whose password contains a slash passed through unfiltered, and an ODBC-style key=value string of the form 'Server=...;Uid=...;Pwd=...;' passed through unfiltered. The canonical postgresql DSN with inline credentials and a slash-free password was correctly dropped, so the control works on the one shape it models.
findings.fix: Relax the password character class to allow slashes (exclude only whitespace and the at-sign) and add a key=value credential heuristic matching password/passwd/pwd/secret/token/api_key followed by '='. Better, invert the control so context carries only values a subclass explicitly declares wire-safe.

findings.title: The SEC-002 leak is still reachable through the exported redact_values API
findings.description: The fix added the safe API (register_sensitive) but kept the unsafe one public. redact_values withdraws its values in its finally block, so an exception escaping the with block is logged after the values are gone - the original SEC-002 shape, verbatim.
findings.evidence: Reproduced at HEAD against a route that exits a 'with redact_values(PAN)' block and then raises with the PAN in the message: the PAN appears in the logged traceback UNREDACTED, [REDACTED] count 0, while the register_sensitive equivalents on the same app were clean. The docstring warns about this, but a docstring is not a guardrail and a future story picking the plausibly-named helper reintroduces a high finding.
findings.fix: Make redact_values delegate to register_sensitive without withdrawing, or withdraw only on a clean exit and keep values bound when the block exits via an exception. Failing that, rename it private and add an architecture test that fails on any src/ caller.

findings.title: GET /metrics is unauthenticated and discloses the full raw path list
findings.description: Anyone can read traffic volume, error rates and - because the label is the raw path (SEC-101) - the verbatim set of URLs other clients requested. At HEAD only /health and /metrics exist so today's disclosure is thin, but once group B/E land resource routes, every /applications/{id}, borrower id or document id that appeared in a URL becomes enumerable by an anonymous reader: an IDOR reconnaissance primitive on a lending platform. It is also a probe oracle, reading back exactly which paths and statuses a scan produced.
findings.evidence: curl -si http://127.0.0.1:8009/metrics returns 200 text/plain with no auth; the body listed every path sent during probing, including the 100k synthetic /applications/<id>/documents paths.
findings.fix: Bind /metrics to a separate internal port or restrict it to the scrape network (deny by default at ingress), or require an auth token; and switch to route templates so ids never become label values. Fixing SEC-101 removes most of the disclosure as a side effect.

findings.title: Frontend dev-dependency advisories: npm reports 1 critical, 1 high, 3 moderate
findings.description: npm audit at HEAD reports 5 vulnerabilities across 320 dependencies (5 prod, 314 dev). The production tree (react, react-dom, decimal.js) is clean; every advisory is in dev tooling (vite, vitest, esbuild, @vitest/mocker, vite-node).
findings.evidence: See dependency_audit for the full advisory table and resolved versions (vite@5.4.21, vitest@2.1.9, esbuild@0.21.5). Assigned medium rather than critical/high because none of these ship in the built artefact and none are reachable from the running application; the npm-critical vitest advisory additionally requires 'vitest --ui', which no script invokes. The residual risk is to a developer workstation running npm run dev - real for the vite fs.deny bypass on this Windows host, but not a production exploit path.
findings.fix: npm audit fix --force requires vite@8/vitest@5 (semver-major) - take that deliberately in a dedicated chore commit, or bump within range and re-audit. Do not run 'vitest --ui' on this tree until vitest >= 3.2.6. Add 'npm audit --audit-level=high' to CI so the posture is measured.

findings.owasp: A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures
findings.title: No committed lockfile - package-lock.json is actively gitignored
findings.description: The lockfile exists on disk (157 KB) but is untracked by rule, not by omission. Consequences: npm ci is impossible so every install re-resolves caret ranges and no two builds are guaranteed identical; there are no integrity hashes pinning artefacts, so a compromised or typosquatted transitive release installs silently; and the SEC-111 posture describes only this machine's resolution, which CI cannot reproduce or verify.
findings.evidence: git ls-files frontend shows no lockfile; git check-ignore -v frontend/package-lock.json returns '.gitignore:49 package-lock.json' (and .gitignore:48 '*.lock' additionally suppresses uv.lock and Cargo.lock).
findings.fix: Remove both patterns from .gitignore, commit frontend/package-lock.json, and use npm ci in CI and init.sh. Apply the same reasoning to the backend's uv.lock.

findings.title: No security headers on any response
findings.description: Live responses carry only date, server, content-length, content-type and x-request-id: no X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, no X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, no CSP, no Referrer-Policy, no HSTS, no Cache-Control: no-store. Low today (JSON/plain-text API with no browser-rendered surface in group A), but /metrics is cacheable by any intermediary and the frontend arrives in a later story.
findings.fix: Add a small security-header middleware in the app factory now, while there is a single mount point.

findings.title: /openapi.json and /docs are exposed unauthenticated
findings.description: FastAPI defaults are kept, and both endpoints return 200 on the live server. Harmless at HEAD (two endpoints); becomes a complete unauthenticated map of the origination API - routes, schemas, field names - as stories land.
findings.fix: Disable in production via settings (docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None) or gate behind auth.

findings.title: /health discloses version and infrastructure state unauthenticated
findings.description: Returns {status, database, version} to anyone. 'version' aids version-specific vulnerability targeting and 'database' reveals backend liveness to an attacker timing an outage. Standard for a liveness probe, hence low.
findings.fix: Keep the public probe minimal ({status}) and expose the detailed payload only on the internal port.

findings.title: Values shorter than 6 characters are silently never redacted
findings.description: _MIN_REDACTABLE_LENGTH = 6 skips short registrations with no warning and no error. PAN (10) and Aadhaar (12) are safe, but an OTP, CVV, 4-digit PIN or short account suffix registered by a future story is silently unprotected - a control that fails open and quietly.
findings.fix: Log a warning (or raise) when a registration is rejected as too short, so the caller learns the value is not protected.

findings.title: The {0,4} separator bound narrows redaction coverage
findings.description: The ReDoS fix means PII rendered with 5 or more separators between characters no longer matches. A correct trade-off and acknowledged in the context pack, but it is a behaviour change callers cannot see from the API.
findings.fix: State the bound in register_sensitive's docstring and keep a test pinning it, so a future widening is a deliberate act.

findings.title: The 200-char cap drops silently, and detail has no cap at all
findings.description: Dropping is the right security choice over truncating - a truncated value still emits its first 200 characters, which is most of a PAN, an Aadhaar or a token. Two residuals: the drop is silent, so a caller relying on context for machine-readable specifics (E4-S4-AC2's threshold_kind/configured_value) loses them with no signal; and detail is scrubbed but uncapped, so an over-long internal message crosses whole.
findings.evidence: A 250-char context value was confirmed dropped from a live 409 envelope; the answer to 'is dropping better or worse than truncating' is better, and it should stay.
findings.fix: Log at DEBUG when a key is dropped, and cap detail as well.

findings.title: The redaction guarantee rests on the root handler being the only sink
findings.description: _install_redaction_filter_everywhere covers root plus loggers registered at configure time, and _route_server_loggers_through_root handles the known uvicorn/gunicorn cases. A logger created after configure_logging() with its own handler and propagate=False - precisely what a library's own dictConfig does, and what uvicorn itself did before this fix - bypasses redaction entirely.
findings.fix: Re-run the installer at app startup after all imports, or move the guarantee into JSONLogFormatter.format so handler topology cannot bypass it.

findings.title: Settings() is re-instantiated on every /health request
findings.description: Each unauthenticated probe constructs a fresh pydantic-settings object, re-reading the environment and any .env file from disk - a small per-request I/O amplification on the one endpoint an attacker can hit freely, and a config-reload race if .env ever changes at runtime.
findings.fix: Build Settings once in the app factory and inject it (FastAPI dependency or module-level singleton).

findings.title: The 422 handler reflects an attacker-controlled field name
findings.description: field is joined from pydantic's loc, which for a dict-typed or extra field contains the client-supplied key, so attacker input is echoed into context.field. Bounded and low risk: it passes through sanitise_context (scrubbed, 200-char cap) and the response is application/json, so there is no XSS sink. Noted only because the handler's docstring promises it never echoes rejected input, and the key half of that input does come back.
findings.fix: Emit only the field path shape or an allow-listed field name.

findings.title: No rate limiting or request throttling anywhere in the stack
findings.description: Group A has no login/reset/OTP endpoint, so the OWASP 'missing rate limiting on auth endpoints' check is not yet applicable. Recorded because throttling is the compensating control absent from SEC-101 and SEC-106, both of which are cheap precisely because nothing limits request rate (a single keep-alive connection sustained ~4,900 req/s in probing).
findings.fix: Add a global throttle at the ingress or in the app factory before auth endpoints land in group B.

refuted_candidates.candidate: SEC-001 ReDoS on a different backtracking shape (the requested alternative axis)
refuted_candidates.evidence: Five different adversarial shapes built against _scrub/_redaction_pattern and scaled over value lengths 8-64: repeated-char value vs alternating char/separator haystack; same with a failing sentinel forcing full backtracking at every position; a value whose characters are all separator-adjacent; a tab/space/hyphen-mixed haystack; a digit value vs a grouped-digit haystack. Every shape stayed under 0.7 ms with linear growth (worst 0.65 ms at n=64). Structural reason: the joined branch's alphabets are disjoint - _SEPARATOR_RUN matches only space, tab and hyphen, and that branch is taken only when the value contains no separator - so at any position the consumable separator run is unique, the match is effectively deterministic, and there is nothing to backtrack over. The re.escape(value) literal branch is a plain literal with no quantifier. A 256 x 504-char values vs 20 KB message stress ran 14.9 ms warm / 28.1 ms cold, i.e. benign polynomial. No ReDoS shape exists on this design. The cache did yield a non-regex DoS, filed honestly as SEC-104.

refuted_candidates.candidate: SEC-004 log injection - CRLF or JSON forgery through X-Request-ID into a JSON log line
refuted_candidates.evidence: Two independent barriers. JSONLogFormatter renders through json.dumps, which escapes quotes, backslashes and every control character below 0x20: an id crafted to close the JSON string and inject a level/message pair produced a line that still parsed as valid JSON with exactly the five expected keys and the payload confined inside the request_id string value. And uvicorn's parser rejects the raw bytes anyway - bare LF, NUL and ESC inside a header value each returned 400 Bad Request before the app was invoked. Terminal-escape injection into a log viewer is blocked by the same two mechanisms.

refuted_candidates.candidate: SEC-005 HTTP response splitting via the echoed X-Request-ID response header
refuted_candidates.evidence: The header is reflected verbatim into MutableHeaders, which is the classic setup, but the inbound value can never contain CR or LF: verified over a raw socket, uvicorn answers 400 Bad Request to a request whose header value embeds a bare LF. With no CRLF source, reflection is contained. What remains is length and trust, filed as SEC-106 and SEC-107.

refuted_candidates.candidate: SEC-002 PII in an exception message bypassing redaction and logged at ERROR
refuted_candidates.disposition: REFUTED - genuinely fixed, verified by execution not by commit message
refuted_candidates.evidence: Against create_app() with a route calling register_sensitive(PAN, AADHAAR) and raising with both in the exception message: status 500, body {"error":"InternalServerError","detail":"internal server error"} with no PII, traceback PRESENT in the logs, PAN absent, Aadhaar absent, two [REDACTED] substitutions, request id on the access line. The threadpool path (a sync def handler, which runs on a context copy) is also clean, so the mutable-set-in-a-contextvar design works as its comment claims. The ordering that makes it work is real: Starlette's ServerErrorMiddleware re-raises after sending the 500, so the exception reaches the middleware's except BaseException while both contextvars are still bound, which is why the traceback is both scrubbed and correlated. Residual filed as SEC-109 (the other, still-exported API).

refuted_candidates.candidate: Credential URI split across two context keys defeating _CREDENTIAL_URI
refuted_candidates.disposition: REFUTED as a separate finding - folded into SEC-108
refuted_candidates.evidence: Splitting a DSN so one key holds the scheme-and-user half and another holds the password-and-host half does egress both halves (neither is a URI alone) and reassembly is trivial, but this requires a developer to deliberately split a connection string across two keys - not a realistic shape and not attacker-influenced. Recorded inside SEC-108 as evidence that the check is per-value and heuristic.

refuted_candidates.candidate: XSS in the new frontend code (unsafe raw HTML rendering)
refuted_candidates.evidence: No dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML, Function( or eval anywhere in the change set. MoneyText.tsx renders the formatted value as JSX text, which React auto-escapes; the prop type is Money | string and the string path passes through Money.fromWire validation before display.

refuted_candidates.candidate: Hardcoded secrets in the change set
refuted_candidates.evidence: A targeted scan of the change set for password/secret/api_key/token/private_key/credential assignments matched only token-named local variables holding contextvar reset tokens (middleware.py:88-89, logging.py:89). Settings sources everything from the environment with a TRUELEND_ prefix and carries no default credential; .env files are gitignored.

refuted_candidates.candidate: SQL injection, command injection, SSRF, path traversal, insecure deserialization
refuted_candidates.evidence: No SQL, no ORM, no subprocess/os.system, no outbound HTTP client, no open(), no pickle/yaml.load anywhere in the change set. Group A ships no Repository or Service layer, so these categories have no reachable sink. The only injection in the diff is SEC-102, into the metrics exposition format.

refuted_candidates.candidate: Cross-request PII bleed from the deliberately-unreset contextvars on the failure path
refuted_candidates.evidence: The failure path resets neither contextvar by design. Uvicorn runs each request/response cycle in its own task, so each gets its own context copy and the leak dies with the task; and the worst case of a shared context would be over-redaction of another line, not exposure. request_id_var is overwritten at entry regardless.

out_of_scope: backend/pyproject.toml - no backend dependency manifest in the change set, so scan step 5 (Python dependency audit) was skipped per scope rules.

Authentication and authorization implementation - group A ships no auth layer, JWT, roles or protected routes, so auth-bypass, IDOR and privilege-escalation have no implementation to review. /health and /metrics being unauthenticated is reported as SEC-110/114/115.
CSRF - no state-changing endpoint and no cookie exists at HEAD.
Pre-existing untouched code outside the change set and its immediate data-flow neighbours.
The canvas-sync and regression-suite-full registry BLOCKs (invocation artefacts per context pack section 5).

scope_read: git diff 14e9487..HEAD -- backend frontend (27 files, +2429 lines)
full content of all 12 production source files and both frontend source files
test files consulted only to establish caller reachability
method.reachability_probe: change-set-scoped grep for register_sensitive / redact_values / AppError( in backend/src/** - no production callers
method.live_server: uv run uvicorn src.api.app:app --port 8009 (per pack section 8, distinct port); exercised with curl --path-as-is, raw socket requests for malformed headers, and http.client keep-alive floods; terminated after probing
in_process_probes: TestClient(create_app(inner)) with throwaway routes on the inner FastAPI app
tracemalloc for per-key retained memory over 200k counter keys
time.perf_counter for regex match, compile and cache timings across five backtracking shapes
lru_cache.cache_info() for hit/miss ratios and post-scope PII retention
method.adversarial_verification: Every candidate BLOCK was put through a find-then-refute pass; nine candidates did not survive and are recorded in refuted_candidates. Uncertainty was resolved toward WARN, not BLOCK.
method.deterministic_results_at_head_not_rerun: Backend 88 tests / ruff / mypy and frontend 18 tests / lint / typecheck were taken as given from context pack section 5 rather than re-run.
